thread:
alex: heads-up — the new dashboard p95 by endpoint is showing a weird dip on /v1/generate for a specific client cohort. digging now, but wanted to flag in case it's a sampling/normalization mismatch.

maya: ok can you paste the chart or query? which cohort?

alex: attaching screenshot in thread (paste) but here's the query we use for rollups: `SELECT quantile(0.95)(latency) BY endpoint, region, client_cohort FROM spans WHERE service='inference'`

sam: that looks fine on the surface. are we sure client_cohort is the same cardinality across routes? last time inconsistent tag values caused rollups to merge.

alex: that's the suspicion — some clients send `cohort=enterprise` vs `cohort=enterprise_v2`. the dashboard currently normalizes cohort with a regex in the dashboard layer, but pctl rollups happen in the TSDB earlier.

maya: ah yeah — normalization at viz layer can't fix previously aggregated t-digests. rollup needs canonicalization before compression.

dana: quick Q: what's the desired behavior for the metric when cohort mapping changes during a rollout? keep them separate, or merge historical?

alex: ideally historical stays canonicalized to the new name for dashboard continuity (we want to avoid p95 flips during canary). but that implies re-ingesting or rewriting rollups. not trivial.

sam: we could apply an alias map at ingestion that maps `enterprise_v2` -> `enterprise` before we t-digest. small window where both will exist though, depending on tag propagation.

maya: ingestion aliasing is doable. downside: we lose the ability to distinguish cohorts during transition unless we add a `raw_cohort` tag preserved for debugging.

dana: preserve `raw_cohort` sounds reasonable. also need to consider quota/routing policies that are cohort-aware — rewrites must not break enforcement.

alex: good call. I noticed this also interacts with routing fallback stats — when route fallback kicks in, endpoint labels differ and cause p50/p95 to jump because counts get split.

sam: that's a separate surface but related. For the percentile correctness: we should add a dashboard calc that shows sample counts by aggregation key alongside pctl values. that will help UX to see when counts drop.

maya: agree. smaller counts = unreliable p99. add a teletype: `count, p50, p95, p99` in the panel title.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for `ingest-normalizer:v1.3.0` — ETA 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC — changelog: add cohort aliasing and preserve raw_cohort tag.

alex: nice. can we also add an alert rule: if p95 shifts >20% and sample_count < 100 within 1h, annotate as "low-sample spike" (do not auto-open incident)?

maya: yes — add as an annotation first. we don't want noisy pager blips.

sam: follow-ups: 1) update docs for how cohort aliasing works, 2) add a one-off job to backfill previous 30d rollups for `enterprise_v2` -> `enterprise` (if storage/t-digest supports rewrite), 3) add note in rollout playbook.

dana: I can take docs + playbook. alex/sam can you own backfill feasibility?

alex: I'll prototype a backfill script that reads rollup blobs, remaps tags, and recomputes t-digests into a new namespace. if it's fast we can run for 30d.

sam: I'll check storage/query load and whether we can run during low-traffic window. if backfill is heavy, fallback is to show viz-layer historical reconciling (less ideal).

maya: thanks all. putting this on the eng-platform board as a short-term bug + long-term backlog item.

alex: thx — will post findings by EOD with sample logs and an example rollup blob.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: `ingest-normalizer:v1.3.0` succeeded — 5 nodes updated.
